name: Battle of Glen Fruin
narrative: The MacGregors defeated the Colquhouns of Luss in a clan battle that led to the proscription of the name MacGregor.
outcome: MacGregor victory; the clan was outlawed by the Privy Council.

name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
narrative: Interlinked wars in England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, from the Bishops' Wars to the battle of Worcester.
outcome: Execution of Charles I (1649) and the Commonwealth.

name: Battle of Newburn
narrative: In the Second Bishops' War the Covenanters forced the Tyne crossing at Newburn and occupied Newcastle.
outcome: Scottish victory; Charles I forced to summon the Long Parliament.

name: Siege of Caerlaverock (1640)
narrative: The royalist earl of Nithsdale held Caerlaverock for thirteen weeks against Covenanters.
outcome: Surrendered on the king's instructions; partly dismantled.

name: Battle of Edgehill
narrative: The first pitched battle of the English Civil War.
outcome: Indecisive; the king later advanced on London but turned back at Turnham Green.

name: Siege of Skipton Castle
narrative: Skipton was blockaded for about three years, one of the longest sieges of the war.

name: Battle of Braddock Down
narrative: Hopton's Cornish army routed the Parliamentarian invaders of Cornwall.

name: Battle of Hopton Heath
participants: Parliamentarians (Sir John Gell, Sir William Brereton)
narrative: An inconclusive battle near Stafford in which the royalist commander Northampton was killed.

name: Battle of Stratton
narrative: Hopton's army stormed the Parliamentarian position on Stamford Hill.

name: Battle of Adwalton Moor
narrative: Newcastle's army defeated the Fairfaxes, giving the royalists control of most of Yorkshire.

name: Battle of Lansdown
narrative: Royalists stormed Waller's position on Lansdown Hill at heavy cost; Sir Bevil Grenville was killed.

name: Battle of Roundway Down
narrative: Royalist cavalry relieving Devizes destroyed Waller's army; many fugitives fell down the steep scarp.

name: Storming of Bristol
narrative: Prince Rupert stormed Bristol, England's second city, with heavy royalist losses.

name: Siege of Gloucester
narrative: Charles I besieged Gloucester until a relief army under the earl of Essex arrived.

name: First Battle of Newbury
narrative: The king tried to block Essex's return to London; Lord Falkland was among the dead.

name: Battle of Winceby
narrative: A cavalry action in which Cromwell's horse routed royalists in Lincolnshire.

name: Battle of Nantwich
narrative: Fairfax relieved Nantwich, defeating royalist troops recently returned from Ireland.

name: Battle of Cheriton
narrative: Waller defeated the royalist army in Hampshire, ending royalist hopes of advancing into the south-east.

name: Bolton Massacre
participants: Parliamentarian garrison and townspeople of Bolton
narrative: Royalist forces stormed Bolton; Parliamentarian pamphlets described the killing of soldiers and civilians.
disagreements: Death figures come from partisan contemporary reports and vary considerably.

name: Battle of Cropredy Bridge
narrative: Waller attacked the strung-out royalist army on the Cherwell and was repulsed.

name: Battle of Marston Moor
participants: Parliamentarians and Scottish Covenanters (Leven, Manchester, Fairfax)
narrative: The largest battle of the English Civil Wars, fought in the evening; Cromwell's cavalry decided the day.
outcome: Decisive allied victory; royalist control of the north collapsed and York surrendered.

name: Battle of Tippermuir
participants: Royalists (marquess of Montrose, Alasdair Mac Colla)
narrative: Montrose's first victory, over a larger but inexperienced Covenanter force.

name: Battle of Aberdeen (Justice Mills)
narrative: Montrose defeated the Covenanters outside Aberdeen; his troops then killed many townspeople.
outcome: Royalist victory followed by the sack of Aberdeen.

name: Battle of Fyvie
narrative: Montrose, caught by Argyll's larger army near Fyvie castle, held a strong position on a hillside and repulsed Covenanter attacks.
outcome: Inconclusive; Montrose withdrew into the hills.

name: Battle of Montgomery
participants: Parliamentarians (Sir John Meldrum, Sir Thomas Myddelton)
narrative: Royalists besieging Parliament's garrison in Montgomery castle were defeated by a relief force; the largest Civil War battle in Wales.

name: Battle of Lostwithiel
narrative: Essex's army was trapped in Cornwall; his cavalry broke out but the infantry surrendered at Fowey.

name: Second Battle of Newbury
narrative: A Parliamentarian pincer attack failed to destroy the king's army.
outcome: Indecisive; the dispute that followed led to the New Model Army.

name: Battle of Inverlochy
participants: Covenanters (Campbells under the marquess of Argyll)
narrative: After a winter flank march Montrose fell on the Campbell army at Inverlochy.

name: Battle of Auldearn
narrative: Montrose defeated a Covenanter attack on his position at Auldearn.

name: Battle of Naseby
participants: New Model Army (Sir Thomas Fairfax, Oliver Cromwell)
narrative: The New Model Army destroyed the king's main field army; the royalist infantry surrendered and the king's papers were captured. Women in the royalist baggage train were killed in the pursuit.

name: Battle of Alford
narrative: Montrose defeated Baillie's army near the Don; Lord Gordon was killed.

name: Battle of Langport
narrative: The New Model Army destroyed Goring's western army.

name: Battle of Kilsyth
narrative: Montrose's greatest victory; the Covenanter infantry was destroyed in the pursuit.
outcome: Royalist victory; Montrose briefly controlled Scotland.

name: Battle of Philiphaugh
narrative: Leslie surprised Montrose's depleted army; prisoners and camp followers were killed afterwards.

name: Battle of Rowton Heath
participants: Royalists (Charles I's horse under Sir Marmaduke Langdale)
narrative: The king, watching from Chester, saw his cavalry defeated while trying to relieve the city.

name: Siege of Basing House
narrative: The fortified mansion of the marquess of Winchester withstood repeated sieges before Cromwell stormed it on 14 October 1645.
outcome: Stormed and destroyed; many defenders killed.

name: Siege of Corfe Castle
narrative: Corfe, defended by Lady Bankes, fell through treachery in February 1646 after a long siege.

name: Battle of Stow-on-the-Wold
narrative: The last royalist field army of the first Civil War was defeated.

name: Siege of Goodrich Castle
narrative: Birch's mortar 'Roaring Meg' bombarded Goodrich into surrender.

name: Siege of Raglan Castle
narrative: One of the last royalist strongholds surrendered after a siege of about thirteen weeks.

name: Surrender of Harlech (1647)
narrative: Harlech was the last royalist castle of the first Civil War to surrender.

name: Battle of St Fagans
narrative: The largest battle in Wales of the Second Civil War; the rebel army was defeated.

name: Siege of Pembroke
narrative: Cromwell besieged Pembroke for about six weeks until the garrison surrendered.

name: Siege of Colchester
participants: Royalists (earl of Norwich, Sir Charles Lucas, Sir George Lisle)
narrative: A royalist army was besieged in Colchester for eleven weeks, with severe hunger among the townspeople.

name: Battle of Preston (1648)
participants: Scottish Engagers and English royalists (duke of Hamilton)
narrative: Cromwell attacked the strung-out invading army at Preston and pursued it south to Warrington.
outcome: Decisive Parliamentarian victory; end of the Second Civil War.

name: Third Siege of Pontefract
narrative: Royalists who had seized Pontefract in 1648 held out until after Charles I's execution.

name: Battle of Carbisdale
narrative: Montrose's final invasion was defeated; he was captured and executed in Edinburgh.

name: Battle of Dunbar (1650)
narrative: Cromwell's army, cornered at Dunbar, attacked at dawn and routed Leslie's army. Thousands of prisoners were marched south; many died, including at Durham.

name: Siege of Edinburgh Castle (1650)
narrative: After Dunbar, Cromwell's forces besieged Edinburgh castle, which surrendered on Christmas Eve.

name: Battle of Inverkeithing
narrative: Lambert's force crossed the Forth and defeated the Scots, outflanking their position at Stirling.

name: Sack of Dundee
narrative: Monck stormed Dundee; soldiers and civilians were killed and the town plundered.
disagreements: Estimates of the dead vary widely and derive from later and partisan accounts; no figure is used.

name: Battle of Worcester
narrative: The final battle of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms; Charles II escaped after the defeat, famously hiding in an oak tree.

name: Siege of Dunnottar Castle
narrative: Dunnottar held out for about eight months; the Honours of Scotland were smuggled out and hidden in Kinneff church.
outcome: Garrison surrendered; the regalia were not found.

name: Battle of Sedgemoor
participants: auth-england:Royal army (earl of Feversham, John Churchill)
narrative: Monmouth's night attack on the royal camp failed; his largely untrained army was destroyed.
outcome: Royal victory; Monmouth executed and the 'Bloody Assizes' followed.

name: Siege of Edinburgh Castle (1689)
narrative: The duke of Gordon held the castle for James VII for three months.

name: Battle of Killiecrankie
narrative: A Highland charge swept away Mackay's army, but Dundee was mortally wounded.

name: Battle of Dunkeld
narrative: The Cameronians held Dunkeld against a Jacobite army in street fighting; much of the town burned.

name: Battle of Cromdale
narrative: Government dragoons surprised the Jacobite camp at dawn.

name: Massacre of Glencoe
narrative: Soldiers billeted with the MacDonalds of Glencoe killed their hosts on government orders after the chief's late oath of allegiance.
outcome: Thirty-eight people were killed; others died of exposure after their homes were burned.

name: Battle of Sheriffmuir
narrative: Each army's right wing routed the opposing left; Mar failed to exploit his numerical advantage.
outcome: Indecisive, but a strategic Jacobite failure.

name: Battle of Preston (1715)
narrative: Jacobites who had marched into England fought from barricades in Preston before surrendering.

name: Bombardment of Eilean Donan
narrative: Royal Navy frigates bombarded the castle, garrisoned by Spanish troops, and then blew it up.

name: Battle of Glen Shiel
narrative: The small Spanish-backed rising of 1719 was defeated in Glen Shiel.

name: Jacobite rising of 1745
narrative: Charles Edward Stuart raised his standard at Glenfinnan, took Edinburgh, invaded England as far as Derby, then retreated to defeat at Culloden.
outcome: Rising crushed; harsh repression in the Highlands followed.

name: Battle of Prestonpans
narrative: A dawn Highland charge routed Cope's army in minutes.

name: Sieges of Carlisle (1745)
narrative: Carlisle surrendered to the Jacobites in November; the garrison they left was forced to surrender to Cumberland on 30 December.
outcome: Retaken by the government; garrison prisoners executed later.

name: Clifton Moor Skirmish
narrative: The Jacobite rearguard checked Cumberland's pursuing cavalry at Clifton.

name: Battle of Falkirk Muir
narrative: Fought in a storm late in the day; Hawley's dragoons were broken by Highland musketry and charge.

name: Battle of Culloden
narrative: The last pitched battle on British soil. The Jacobite army was destroyed in under an hour by artillery and musketry; many wounded and fugitives were killed afterwards.
outcome: Decisive government victory; end of the '45.
